summary: Object-oriented language prioritizing developer happiness, elegant DSLs, and convention-over-configuration web development.

rows.means: defines a method with optional default parameters
rows.consequence: In Ruby, the last evaluated expression is automatically returned without requiring an explicit return keyword.

rows.means: print with newline / print without newline / inspect with debug quotes
rows.consequence: p object calls object.inspect, displaying quotes on strings and showing internal array structures, ideal for debugging.

rows.means: instance state / class-shared state / global variable / immutable symbol
rows.consequence: Symbols (:name) are immutable, internalized strings. Ruby allocates only one memory address per symbol name.

rows.means: generates getter and setter methods automatically
rows.consequence: attr_reader generates only getters; attr_writer generates only setters; attr_accessor creates both.

rows.means: chunks of code passed into methods to execute
rows.consequence: Use { ... } for single-line blocks; use do ... end for multi-line blocks. The bedrock of Ruby's functional enumerables.

rows.means: pauses method execution to execute the passed block
rows.consequence: Allows writing custom iteration methods and wrappers: def benchmark; t = Time.now; yield; Time.now - t; end.

rows.means: defines a class inheriting from a superclass
rows.consequence: In Ruby, classes are open: you can reopen any existing class (even String) and add new methods at runtime (monkey patching).

rows.code: nil and nil? / empty? / blank? / present?
rows.means: the singleton null object and state check helpers
rows.consequence: In Ruby, ONLY false and nil are falsy. The number 0 and empty string "" are truthy! blank? is a Rails helper checking for whitespace.

rows.means: executes the block only if condition evaluates to false
rows.consequence: Idiomatic opposite of if. Often used as an inline guard clause: return if user.nil? or redirect_to login unless logged_in?.

rows.means: refers to the current executing object or class context
rows.consequence: Inside a class method definition (def self.find_by_email), self refers to the Class object itself.
Executes lazily: chaining query methods builds an ActiveRecord::Relation; SQL executes only when records are accessed.

rows.means: declares relational database foreign key relationships
rows.consequence: Automatically injects helper methods like user.orders and order.user, handling SQL joins behind the scenes.

rows.means: calls methods only if the receiver is not nil
rows.consequence: Returns nil safely if any link in the chain is nil, preventing NoMethodError: undefined method for nil:NilClass.
numbers.select(&:even?) uses the symbol-to-proc trick (&:method) to call .even? on every item in the list.
